informal_statement: The function \( b^x \) is a convex function for all real numbers \( x \) when \( b \) is a positive real number.
informal_proof:
First, we note that for any positive real number \( b \), the function \( b^x \) can be rewritten as \( \exp(\ln(b) \cdot x) \) because \( b = e^{\ln(b)} \).

The exponential function \( \exp(x) \) is known to be convex, and multiplying the argument \( x \) by a constant \( \ln(b) \) (which is real since \( b > 0 \)) results in an affine transformation of \( x \). Affine transformations preserve convexity, so \( \ln(b) \cdot x \) is also convex.

Finally, since the composition of convex functions remains convex, and \( \exp(\ln(b) \cdot x) = b^x \), it follows that \( b^x \) is convex for all real numbers \( x \).

id.content:
theorem ConvexOn_rpow_left (b : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) :
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (fun (x : ℝ) => b ^ x) := by
  have : (fun x => b ^ x) = (Real.exp ∘ (Real.log b * ·)) := by
    ext x
    simp only [comp_apply]
    rw [<-Real.rpow_def_of_pos hb]
  rw [this]
  exact ConvexOn.comp_linearMap convexOn_exp (LinearMap.mul ℝ ℝ (Real.log b))

C1_dependencies.name: LinearMap.mul
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The multiplication in a non-unital non-associative algebra is a bilinear map.

A weaker version of this for semirings exists as `AddMonoidHom.mul`. -/
@[simps!]
def mul : A →ₗ[R] A →ₗ[R] A :=
  LinearMap.mk₂ R (· * ·) add_mul smul_mul_assoc mul_add mul_smul_comm

C1_dependencies.name: ConvexOn.comp_linearMap
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- If `g` is convex on `s`, so is `(f ∘ g)` on `f ⁻¹' s` for a linear `f`. -/
theorem ConvexOn.comp_linearMap {f : F → β} {s : Set F} (hf : ConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (g : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) :
    ConvexOn 𝕜 (g ⁻¹' s) (f ∘ g) :=
  ⟨hf.1.linear_preimage _, fun x hx y hy a b ha hb hab =>
    calc
      f (g (a • x + b • y)) = f (a • g x + b • g y) := by rw [g.map_add, g.map_smul, g.map_smul]
      _ ≤ a • f (g x) + b • f (g y) := hf.2 hx hy ha hb hab⟩
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:
/-- If `g` is convex on `s`, so is `(f ∘ g)` on `f ⁻¹' s` for a linear `f`. -/
theorem ConvexOn.comp_linearMap {f : F → β} {s : Set F} (hf : ConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (g : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) :
    ConvexOn 𝕜 (g ⁻¹' s) (f ∘ g) :=
  ⟨hf.1.linear_preimage _, fun x hx y hy a b ha hb hab =>
    calc
      f (g (a • x + b • y)) = f (a • g x + b • g y) := by rw [g.map_add, g.map_smul, g.map_smul]
      _ ≤ a • f (g x) + b • f (g y) := hf.2 hx hy ha hb hab⟩

  rw [rpow_def_of_nonneg (le_of_lt hx), if_neg (ne_of_gt hx)]

C1_dependencies.name: Real.log
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The real logarithm function, equal to the inverse of the exponential for `x > 0`,
to `log |x|` for `x < 0`, and to `0` for `0`. We use this unconventional extension to
`(-∞, 0]` as it gives the formula `log (x * y) = log x + log y` for all nonzero `x` and `y`, and
the derivative of `log` is `1/x` away from `0`. -/
@[pp_nodot]
noncomputable def log (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if hx : x = 0 then 0 else expOrderIso.symm ⟨|x|, abs_pos.2 hx⟩

C1_dependencies.name: Set.univ
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The universal set on a type `α` is the set containing all elements of `α`.

This is conceptually the "same as" `α` (in set theory, it is actually the same), but type theory
makes the distinction that `α` is a type while `Set.univ` is a term of type `Set α`. `Set.univ` can
itself be coerced to a type `↥Set.univ` which is in bijection with (but distinct from) `α`. -/
def univ : Set α := {_a | True}

C1_dependencies.name: ConvexOn
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Convexity of functions -/
def ConvexOn : Prop :=
  Convex 𝕜 s ∧ ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → ∀ ⦃y⦄, y ∈ s → ∀ ⦃a b : 𝕜⦄, 0 ≤ a → 0 ≤ b → a + b = 1 →
    f (a • x + b • y) ≤ a • f x + b • f y
